questions.question: What is observed at the cathode during electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide?
options: Silvery globules of molten metal that float to the surface
Bubbles of brown gas with a pungent smell
Colourless gas that burns with a pop sound
Greenish-yellow gas with a choking smell
questions.explanation: In molten PbBr₂, Pb²⁺ ions are attracted to the cathode and gain electrons: Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb. Molten lead metal appears as silvery globules that float to the surface due to lower density.

questions.question: Which half-equation represents the reaction at the anode during electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
options: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na
4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻
2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻
2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂
questions.explanation: In molten NaCl, only Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions are present. Cl⁻ ions are attracted to the anode and lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻, producing chlorine gas.

questions.question: Why must the electrolyte be molten or in aqueous solution for electrolysis to occur?
options: The ions need to be mobile to carry electric charge
The compound must be heated to break covalent bonds
Water is needed to provide H⁺ and OH⁻ ions
The electrodes only work at high temperatures
questions.explanation: Electrolysis requires mobile ions to carry electric charge through the electrolyte. In solid ionic compounds, ions are fixed in position. Melting or dissolving allows ions to move freely.

questions.question: What product is formed at the cathode during extraction of aluminium from molten aluminium oxide?
options: Oxygen gas
Carbon dioxide gas
Aluminium oxide vapour
Aluminium metal
questions.explanation: In the extraction of aluminium, Al³⁺ ions are reduced at the cathode: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. Molten aluminium metal collects at the bottom of the electrolytic cell.

questions.question: Which statement correctly explains why cryolite is added to aluminium oxide in the extraction of aluminium?
options: Cryolite lowers the melting point and increases conductivity
Cryolite acts as a catalyst to speed up the reaction
Cryolite prevents oxidation of the aluminium produced
Cryolite provides additional aluminium ions for the reaction
questions.explanation: Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) serves two purposes: 1) Lowers the melting point of Al₂O₃ from 2045°C to about 950°C, saving energy. 2) Increases electrical conductivity of the molten mixture.

questions.question: What is observed at the anode during electrolysis of molten calcium chloride?
options: Silvery metal deposits on the electrode
Colourless gas that relights a glowing splint
Brown vapour that condenses to a liquid
Greenish-yellow gas with a pungent smell
questions.explanation: In molten CaCl₂, Cl⁻ ions are oxidised at the anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Chlorine gas is greenish-yellow with a characteristic pungent, choking smell.

questions.question: Which half-equation represents the reduction reaction during electrolysis of molten magnesium oxide?
options: Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Mg
O²⁻ → ½O₂ + 2e⁻
Mg → Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻
½O₂ + 2e⁻ → O²⁻
questions.explanation: Reduction occurs at the cathode. Mg²⁺ ions gain electrons to form magnesium metal: Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Mg. This is the reduction half-equation.

questions.question: Why are graphite electrodes commonly used in electrolysis of molten compounds?
options: Graphite conducts electricity better than metals
Graphite is cheap and does not react with most products
Graphite dissolves in the molten electrolyte
Graphite provides additional carbon for the reaction
questions.explanation: Graphite is inert (unreactive) under most electrolysis conditions, conducts electricity well, and is relatively inexpensive. It does not interfere with the electrolysis products.

questions.question: What mass of chlorine gas is produced at the anode when 2 moles of electrons pass through molten sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: From 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻, 2 moles of electrons produce 1 mole of Cl₂. Molar mass of Cl₂ = 2 × 35.5 = 71.0 g. Therefore, 71.0 g of chlorine gas is produced.

questions.question: What is the main product formed at the cathode during electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
options: Sodium metal
Chlorine gas
Hydrogen gas
Sodium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Electrolysis of molten NaCl produces sodium metal at the cathode (Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na). Sodium hydroxide is only produced during electrolysis of aqueous NaCl.

questions.question: During electrolysis of molten potassium iodide, what is formed at the cathode?
options: Iodine vapour with purple colour
Hydrogen gas from water impurities
Oxygen gas from oxide impurities
Potassium metal that reacts violently with moisture
questions.explanation: K⁺ ions are reduced at the cathode: K⁺ + e⁻ → K. Potassium metal is highly reactive and must be collected under inert conditions to prevent reaction with air or moisture.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the movement of ions during electrolysis?
options: Cations move to the anode, anions move to the cathode
Both cations and anions move to the cathode
Cations move to the cathode, anions move to the anode
Ions do not move; electrons carry the current
questions.explanation: During electrolysis, positively charged cations are attracted to the negative cathode, while negatively charged anions are attracted to the positive anode.

questions.question: What is the main reason electrolysis of molten compounds requires high temperatures?
options: To increase the rate of electron transfer
To melt the ionic compound and allow ion mobility
To reduce the voltage needed for the reaction
To prevent the electrodes from corroding
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds have high melting points due to strong electrostatic forces. High temperatures are needed to melt the solid and allow ions to move freely for electrolysis.

questions.question: Which product is NOT formed during electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide?
options: Aluminium metal at the cathode
Oxygen gas at the anode
Carbon dioxide from anode reaction
Hydrogen gas from water reduction
questions.explanation: Molten Al₂O₃ electrolysis produces Al at cathode and O₂ at anode. The carbon anodes react with oxygen to form CO₂. No water is present, so no hydrogen gas is formed.

questions.question: What is the oxidation half-equation for electrolysis of molten zinc chloride?
options: Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Zn
Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻
2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻
Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻
questions.explanation: Oxidation occurs at the anode. Cl⁻ ions lose electrons to form chlorine gas: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. This is the oxidation half-equation.

questions.question: Why is electrolysis used to extract aluminium from its ore rather than reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium oxide has a very high melting point
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Carbon reduction produces toxic gases
Electrolysis is cheaper than carbon reduction
questions.explanation: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon in the reactivity series. Carbon cannot reduce aluminium oxide to aluminium metal, so electrolysis is the only viable extraction method.

questions.question: During electrolysis of molten copper(II) bromide, what colour change is observed?
options: The molten compound turns from brown to colourless
The cathode turns blue from copper deposition
No visible colour change occurs
Brown bromine vapour is seen at the anode
questions.explanation: Bromide ions are oxidised at the anode: 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻. Bromine vapour is reddish-brown and may be observed as a coloured vapour at the anode.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect the products of electrolysis of a molten compound?
options: The nature of the ions present in the melt
The material of the electrodes used
The concentration of the electrolyte
The voltage applied to the electrodes
questions.explanation: In molten electrolysis, only the ions from the compound are present. Concentration is not a variable as in aqueous solutions. Products depend on ion nature, electrode material, and sufficient voltage.

questions.question: What is the main environmental concern with the electrolytic extraction of aluminium?
options: Release of chlorine gas into the atmosphere
Production of toxic heavy metal waste
High energy consumption and carbon emissions
Depletion of bauxite ore reserves
questions.explanation: The extraction process requires very high temperatures and large amounts of electricity. If the electricity comes from fossil fuels, this results in significant carbon dioxide emissions.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares electrolysis of molten NaCl versus aqueous NaCl?
options: Both produce chlorine gas at the anode only
Aqueous NaCl produces sodium hydroxide at the cathode
Both produce sodium metal at the cathode
Molten NaCl produces sodium; aqueous produces hydrogen
questions.explanation: In molten NaCl, Na⁺ is reduced to Na metal. In aqueous NaCl, H⁺ from water is preferentially reduced over Na⁺ (since H is below Na in reactivity series), producing H₂ gas instead.
